changes.why: Misspelt: 'açık hava' is two words in Turkish, the fused form does not exist. 'Doğa' (as in 'doğa sporları') is one word and covers sport out in the open.
'Gereçler' alone just means 'equipment' (reads like tools/workshop, close to 1603). 'Mutfak' is the word a teenager uses for kitchen things (mutfak eşyaları).
Confusingly close to 103 'Çiftlik' (one letter pattern apart). 'Evlilik' also fits the scope better: husband and wife, weddings, living together.
Confusingly close to 2601 'Yarışlar' (same stem, two letters apart). 'Turnuva' is distinct and covers duels, tournaments, trophies and podiums.
Apostrophe-free alternative exists; 'Екскурсії' is common and covers sightseeing with guides, maps and souvenirs, not only the monuments.
